title: Glessner's 18th Street roof now meets the stable cupola level
items: The ridge of Glessner House's 18th Street wing is about 2 ft higher. It now runs level into the stable's ridge at the little cupola, as the 1963 survey photograph and today's aerial views show, instead of stepping down.
The stone gable on the alley side of the stable now sits on its roof, with its coping just above the ridge tiles, instead of standing over the roof like a fin.
The courtyard dining tower's copper cap keeps its height; its short tiled ridge now runs back into the raised roof.
